title: Kian's Dry Boat Parade
markdown:
OH! OH! OH! Get ready for measuring, splashing, and staying super-duper dry! This is about Kian! Kian LOVES to measure things – how tall a flower is, or how many fluffy clouds puff up. His best friend is Puddle, a bouncy green frog who just loves to ribbit-ribbit and hop! And then there’s Grandma Nell, with her warm hugs and brilliant ideas!

Kian, Puddle, and Grandma Nell were planning a teeny boat parade! They’d build little boats from leaves and twigs and float them down the sparkly stream. "This will be the most amazingest parade EVER!" croaked Puddle. But then Puddle looked at the stream. His big froggy eyes blinked. "Kian," he squeaked, "what if water splashes? Our passengers will be… all wet and drippy!"

Wet and drippy passengers? Oh, what a pickle! Their first idea was a big leaf roof. WHOOSH! A little wave splashed over it. Nope, not dry enough. Next, a fluffy dandelion puff. SPLISH! SPLASH! It got all mushy – yucky mushy! "This is tricky-tricky-tricky!" wriggled Puddle.

"Hmm," hummed Kian, tapping his chin. "We need something water just can't get through! Something that stays dry!" He remembered Grandma Nell’s bright red umbrella and her shiny green boots. "Grandma Nell!" he called. "Can you help us find something that keeps our passengers super dry?" Grandma Nell smiled her warmest smile. "Of course! Let’s look closely. We need to find things that don't let water through!"

So, the three friends went on a special trip! They found a smooth, waxy fabric, a fuzzy bit of wool, and a crinkly plastic wrapper. Kian got his measuring tape ready. "It's time for an experiment!" he grinned. Grandma Nell got a little watering can.

"Let's see!" said Grandma Nell. She poured water onto the fuzzy wool. Swoooooosh! The water soaked right in, like a thirsty sponge. It felt heavy and damp. "Brrr! Nope," croaked Puddle. Next, water on the waxy fabric. Drip, drip, plop! The water rolled right off! "Ooooh!" exclaimed Kian. "It’s like the water can’t stick!" Suddenly, Kian understood. That's when it clicked! Finally, water on the plastic wrapper. Squelch, squelch! The water beaded up and rolled away. "Hooray!" cheered Puddle. "Both of those keep the water out! We have winners!"

They chose the shiny, waxy fabric. Kian measured it perfectly. They shaped it into a snug roof for their boat. When they put the boat on the water, it floated! They placed a brave little ladybug inside. Splish! A little wave splashed the boat. But guess what? Not a single drop of water got to the ladybug! She stayed perfectly, wonderfully dry. "YESSSSS!" shouted Kian, doing a happy dance. Puddle did a super-bouncy hop. "Our parade is saved! It will be the driest, bestest parade EVER!"

Kian beamed. "You see, Puddle?" he explained. "Some materials are like tiny walls for water. The little holes are too small for water to get through, or they're super slippery, so water slides right off!" Grandma Nell nodded. "Exactly! It’s called being waterproof. It’s how the material is made and how it acts with water." Puddle wiggled his toes. "Wow! So that's why your boots keep your feet dry, Grandma Nell!" Kian giggled. "Yup! I wonder what other amazing things in the world work this way?" And as the sun shone, their tiny boat parade began, with all passengers perfectly dry, ready for a splashingly good time!
characters: Kian the measure master, Puddle the frog, Grandma Nell
